author: Joseph Volpe Sun staff writer
title: Hopkinton police car show returns to benefit Maddie Potts Foundation | News | thewesterlysun.com
text:
HOPKINTON — After raising more than $5,000 for the Maddie Potts Foundation and drawing over 300 cars last year, the Hopkinton Police Department is hoping to make its second annual car show even bigger, with a goal of bringing in 500 cars for this year’s event.
The department will be hosting its second car show, with all proceeds directly supporting the Maddie Potts Foundation on Saturday, Sept. 12 at Crandall Field, with brand new award categories for this year’s show. The show will begin at noon and end at 4 p.m., with judging commencing at 1:30 p.m.
Hopkinton Police Chief Mark Carrier said that last year’s car show supporting the Maddie Potts Foundation was a great success, with more than 300 cars attending the show. He said this upcoming car show is one of the department’s major events, with the other being Race of Raymond, which is held in the spring.
Hopkinton Public Welfare Director Tina Lavigne said that the car show last year raised more than $5,000 for the Potts Foundation, which Carrier said far exceeded their expectations and were heart warmed to see the overwhelming amount of support from the community.
The Maddie Potts Foundation was started in November 2017 after Maddie’s sudden death on the Chariho soccer field due to an acutely ruptured brain aneurysm. The 501(c)(3) nonprofit strives to carry her message of kindness, compassion and hard work, now trademarked as “Maddie Mentality.” The foundation focuses on giving back to the community through scholarships and support for individuals and their families experiencing acute loss.
“The Maddie Potts Foundation is such a strong foundation and Stephanie and Dan Potts are tremendous members and supporters of our community,” Carrier said. “The foundation has helped so many other people, so whatever we can do to help them out, we’re going to do it. Hopefully we can get 500 cars this year. If we can pull that off, that would be great.”
Those who want to show off their car in the show do not need to pre-register, and the entry cost is $20 per vehicle. Spectators can enter for free, and there will be food trucks available from local businesses such as South County Barbeque and W’s Wood Fired Pizza Oven.
Lavigne, who organizes many local car shows, said that this year the awards will be given out to car show participants, with the main categories being Best in Show (judged), People’s Choice, Sponsor’s Choice, and Chief’s Choice.
Other categories will include a variety of awards including Best Vintage (pre 1960), Best Classic (1960-1989), Best Modern (1990-present), Best Trucks, Best Hot Rod, Best Import/Tuner, and Best Stock.
Carrier additionally said this is a good opportunity to meet some of the local Hopkinton police officers, and interact with them in a positive community event environment.
Lavigne has been advising the Hopkinton Police Department about how to run the show and helped come up with the trophies and categories for the cars, along with coordinating with other town departments such as the Department of Public Works to assist in parking and traffic control.
This week is the last chance for vendors to register, with a pre-registration fee of $100 and a max tent size of 10x20. Vendors can email ryan.percival@hopkintonpoliceri.gov.
